name: Cement
intro: Cement is the largest group on the SMART client list: more than 20 Indian cement groups and plants in Egypt and Bangladesh (2014 list) [[NEEDS CLIENT: updated count]]. SMART phones, PA systems and bag counters work on loading lines and plant floors where dust and noise defeat ordinary equipment.
problems: Dust and plant noise drown out an ordinary phone bell. WMHS-III and WMHS-IIIWP cancel background noise at the mouthpiece, and TR-III and FL-III make incoming calls heard and seen.
A team spread over a large plant needs paging, not just a call. MCS-II (loops up to 2000 m) and MCS-III give individual, zone and all-call paging.
Miscounted bags at truck and wagon loading. SMART bag counters hold a set count, warn at the last 10 bags and can stop the conveyor or loader.

name: Steel & Metals
intro: Steel is one of the three core industries SMART has served, alongside cement and power. Our 2014 list includes SAIL, Tata Steel, Jindal Stainless and copper and aluminium producers [[NEEDS CLIENT: updated count]].
problems: Shop floors so loud that a normal ring is never heard. WMHS-IIILH adds a 40 W loud ringer and a xenon flasher, and TR-III and FL-III fit any SMART phone.
Crane operators cut off by height and moving structures. CAS-HF announces over a walkie-talkie link, and CCS-HF links the cabin to up to 5 points on the crane.
Alarms that must reach a whole bay. EH-FL pairs a 107 dB hooter with a red LED flasher, and ISAS plays recorded or live announcements across the plant.

name: Power
intro: Power is one of the three core industries SMART has served, alongside cement and steel. Line-powered phones, PA systems and hotlines connect the control room with field and outdoor posts [[NEEDS CLIENT: updated count]].
problems: Outdoor posts in rain and dust. WMHS-IIIWP is fully line powered in a cast-aluminium canopy housing, so there is no local supply to fail.
The control room needs a direct line to key posts. HT-I rings up to 4 phones on one pair, and HT-IP links two sites over single-mode fibre up to 10 km.
Announcements must reach the whole site. MCS-II and MCS-III give zone and all-call paging, and ISAS repeats recorded safety messages on a timer.

name: Pharma & Clean Rooms
intro: Clean rooms need phones that sit flush and work hands-free. SMART clean room phones serve packing cubicles, sampling and dispensing areas, labs and pharmaceutical units, in analogue and SIP versions.
problems: Wall phones that stick out in a clean room. Every CR model mounts flush and keeps to one AUTO DIAL key and a 4 × 3 keypad.
Surfaces cleaned with solvents. CR-III-SS has a full stainless steel body and an SS 304 front under a solvent-resistant overlay.
Plants moving to VoIP. CR-IP is a SIP phone powered over Ethernet, and CR-III-IP brings the CR-III layout to an existing VoIP network.

name: Fertiliser & Chemicals
intro: Fertiliser and chemical plants combine corrosive air, outdoor process areas and alarms that must be understood. SMART supplies stainless steel bag counters, weatherproof phones and voice alarms to these sites [[NEEDS CLIENT: updated count]].
problems: Corrosive urea and fertiliser atmospheres. BC-L-SS puts the bag counter and its sensing head in 304-grade stainless steel.
A siren alone does not say what went wrong. VA-1 and the multi-channel voice alarm play a recorded message for each relay contact until the fault clears.
Process areas exposed to weather. WMHS-IIIWP and WMHS-IIWP put line-powered or PA phones in cast-aluminium canopy housings.

name: Ports & Highways
intro: Highways, ports and docks need SOS points where there is no cable and a control room that knows who is calling. SMART emergency call boxes run on GSM or VoIP, with solar options, and report to a central rack and software.
problems: No cable along the route. GSM-ECB BOX works on any GSM SIM network and runs on solar power with battery backup.
The control room must know which box is calling and that every box works. The ECB server rack and HTMS show caller ID with location, record every call and check boxes automatically.
Remote posts at ports and docks. WMHF-IIIGSM is a vandal-resistant GSM phone with solar and battery options.

metaDescription: SMART for highways, ports and docks: solar GSM and VoIP emergency call boxes, a control-room server rack and software with caller ID and recording.

name: Rail & Metro
intro: Track lines, tunnels and stations need emergency phones that live outdoors and fit the network in place. SMART rail telephones come in line-powered analogue and SIP versions in IP 65 die-cast aluminium. [[NEEDS CLIENT: rail and metro references and any RDSO approvals]]
problems: Trackside phones exposed to weather. WMHS-ERT-A and WMHS-ERT-I sit in IP 65 aluminium die-cast housings.
Networks moving to IP. WMHS-ERT-I is a SIP phone for any standard IP PABX; WMHS-ERT-A works on any two-wire line.
Stations and lines that need SOS points without new cable. GSM-ECB BOX and VOIP-ECB give one-button hands-free calls to the control room.
metaDescription: SMART for rail and metro: IP 65 die-cast emergency rail telephones in analogue and SIP versions, plus GSM and VoIP emergency call boxes for stations.

name: Mining
intro: Mines need phones and signals that cope with dust, water and noise, and call points where there is no cable. SMART line-powered phones, GSM call points and hooters are listed for mines [[NEEDS CLIENT: updated count]].
problems: Dust, water and noise. WMHS-III and WMHS-IIIWP are line powered, with noise-cancelling handsets and sealed keypads.
Remote mine locations without cabling. WMHF-IIIGSM and GSM-ECB BOX work on any GSM SIM network with solar options.
Warning and evacuation signals. EH gives six siren tones at 100 W, and EH-FL adds a red LED flasher visible from 100 m.
